name: Egg Hunt
label: Dischord
lede: Two Minor Threat founders, a 24-track studio in a North London garage, one Easter weekend, and the last music Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson ever recorded together.

hero.by: Photo: Egghunt Cynthia Connolly / Dischord Records

eras.title: Easter in Wood Green
eras.text: In spring 1986 Embrace was over and Minor Threat was two and a half years gone. Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson, who ran Dischord, went to England, and a visit to Southern Records turned into an Easter session that became Dischord's twentieth release.

years.h: Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson go to London
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] fly to England, on Dischord distribution business according to Wikipedia. [[John Loder|39baeee6-dc33-470e-a62d-099c89463590]] of Southern Records invites them to record while they're in town.

years.h: Egg Hunt's Me and You: a basement song, finally on tape
years.p: Dischord says Me and You was something Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson had played together in the basement for many years. The two had been making music together since the Teen Idles in 1979.

years.h: We All Fall Down: the song Embrace passed on
years.p: Ian MacKaye wrote We All Fall Down for [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], and Embrace said no. In London it becomes Egg Hunt's B-side.

years.h: Egg Hunt tries to become a band
years.p: Back in D.C., Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson try to build a full band with [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]]'s [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] and [[Steve Niles|ce17b293-3129-426d-b9d3-7403dfda4d8f]], but in Dischord's words it wasn't meant to be. MacKaye leaves, and Nelson, Turner and Niles become Three.

years.h: 2 Songs: Egg Hunt's Easter session in London, released
years.p: Over Easter weekend 1986, Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson recorded four songs in John Loder's garage studio in Wood Green. Two came out that October as Dischord No. 20, the last music the pair recorded together.
years.xp:
Southern ran out of a row house in Wood Green with a 24-track studio in the garage. Wikipedia gives the session dates as March 27, 28 and 30, with Loder engineering; Easter Sunday fell on March 30, which is where the name came from.

MacKaye sings and plays guitar and bass, his recording debut as a guitarist per Wikipedia. Nelson plays drums and, in Dischord's credits, gum.

Dischord says they had such a good time in London that they decided to release a single to mark the occasion. Only two of the four songs came out, and the partnership that built the [[Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]], [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and Dischord itself ends on record with a holiday single.

eras.title: Two roads out of the garage
eras.text: Egg Hunt never became a band, so the story moves to what Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson did next. They kept running Dischord together, and made music apart.

years.p: Fugazi plays its first show that September. Ian MacKaye sings and plays guitar, the instrument he first recorded on at Southern in Wood Green.

years.h: Jeff Nelson's band Three releases its album after splitting
years.p: Jeff Nelson drums in Three, the band that grew out of the Egg Hunt tryouts. Three's album Dark Days Coming comes out on Dischord after the band has split.

eras.title: A holiday single that keeps coming back
eras.text: Egg Hunt's 2 Songs, recorded over one Easter weekend, kept getting reissued, and kept finding people who had never heard of the band.

years.h: Egg Hunt's 2 Songs on CD for the first time
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Egg Hunt's single is reissued on CD.

years.h: Me and You on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: Egg Hunt's A-side gets a place on Dischord's anniversary box set, 20 Years of Dischord.

years.h: Egg Hunt's 2 Songs back on light blue vinyl
years.p: Wikipedia says Dischord re-releases Egg Hunt's 7-inch on light blue vinyl.
